prompt:
You are a rigorous analyst working for a technology watch team.

DECISION QUESTION:
D'ici 12 mois, une entreprise de services numériques peut-elle s'appuyer sur les résultats des benchmarks d'agents LLM (SWE-bench, WebArena, etc.) pour confier des tâches de développement de routine à des agents autonomes, ou ces scores surestiment-ils leur fiabilité réelle, ce qui impose de se limiter à des expérimentations contrôlées ?

SUB-QUESTIONS:
- SQ1: Que mesurent réellement les benchmarks d'agents, et quelles sont leurs limites (contamination des données, tâches peu réalistes) ?
- SQ2: Quel écart observe-t-on entre scores publiés, évaluations indépendantes et retours d'expérience réels ?
- SQ3: Quelles approches d'agents (planification, mémoire, outils, multi-agents) sont réellement matures ?
- SQ4: Quels échecs et risques sont documentés (fiabilité, injection de prompt, actions destructrices) ?
- SQ5: Où les affirmations des fournisseurs divergent-elles des sources indépendantes ?

TASK: read the DOCUMENT below and extract at most 5 claims that help answer the decision question.
If the document is not useful for the question, return [].

RULES (mandatory):
1. "citation": copy ONE passage VERBATIM from the document: the exact same characters, 1 or 2 consecutive
   sentences, between 30 and 300 characters. Never paraphrase, never translate, never merge separate passages,
   never use "...". If you cannot quote a passage that supports the claim, do not output the claim.
2. "texte": the claim restated in FRENCH, in one sentence, faithful to the citation, adding nothing.
3. "categorie", one of:
   - "fait": verifiable fact or measured result
   - "interpretation": opinion, analysis or conclusion of the author
   - "lacune": missing evidence, unknown, limitation of what has been measured
   - "risque": documented failure, incident or risk
   - "signal": weak signal or emerging trend
4. "theme", one of:
   - "performance_benchmark": scores and results reported on agent benchmarks (SWE-bench, WebArena...)
   - "validite_benchmark": what benchmarks really measure: contamination, realism, flawed tests, gaming
   - "usage_reel": results in real-world use, production deployments, field feedback, productivity
   - "fiabilite_securite": failures, errors, destructive actions, prompt injection, security and safety
   - "maturite_approches": maturity of agent techniques: planning, memory, tool use, multi-agent
   - "supervision_humaine": need for human review, oversight, controlled pilots, governance
5. "position" with respect to the question:
   - "optimiste": supports that agents / benchmark scores are reliable enough for routine development tasks
   - "critique": suggests scores overestimate real reliability, or documents failures, risks or limits
   - "neutre": neither
6. "sous_question": "SQ1" to "SQ5", or null.

Answer with JSON only: a list of objects with keys "texte", "citation", "categorie", "theme", "position", "sous_question".

DOCUMENT
Title: SWE-Bench ProMax: Benchmarking Agents on Large-Scale Multilingual Code Refactoring
Source: arXiv (publication), published 2026-08-10
Text:
"""
As AI coding agents take on increasingly complex, long-horizon software engineering tasks, existing benchmarks are rapidly saturating and their evaluation quality has come under serious scrutiny: a recent audit found that nearly 60% of unsolved SWE-bench Verified instances contain flawed tests -- either overly narrow tests that reject correct solutions or overly broad tests that check unstated requirements -- and that frontier models can verbatim reproduce gold patches from training data. Code refactoring, which requires coordinated, behavior-preserving changes across many files, offers a substantially harder and more realistic test of agent capability, yet remains underserved by current benchmarks. We introduce SWE-Bench ProMax, an expert-curated, multilingual code refactoring benchmark of 170 instances drawn from real commits across seven programming languages (Python, Java, TypeScript, Go, C, C++, and Rust). Every instance undergoes rigorous, multi-stage curation that directly addresses the quality problems identified in prior benchmarks: issue descriptions are rewritten from scratch to provide precise, unambiguous specifications, and test suites are manually reviewed to remove overly narrow and overly broad tests. Tasks with insufficient complexity or limited cross-file scope are filtered out, yielding a benchmark of challenging, large-scale refactoring tasks that average 11.5 modified files and 261.6 lines of code per instance, substantially exceeding the scale of existing benchmarks. Experiments with frontier models under two agent scaffolds show that the best model achieves only 41.2% resolve rate, confirming that SWE-Bench ProMax presents a meaningful and unsaturated challenge for current AI coding agents. Our benchmark is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/swe-bench-promax/SWE-Bench-ProMax.
"""

reponse.texte: Selon un audit récent, près de 60 % des instances non résolues de SWE-bench Verified contiennent des tests défectueux et certains modèles de pointe peuvent reproduire textuellement des correctifs issus de leurs données d'entraînement.
reponse.citation: a recent audit found that nearly 60% of unsolved SWE-bench Verified instances contain flawed tests -- either overly narrow tests that reject correct solutions or overly broad tests that check unstated requirements -- and that frontier models can verbatim reproduce gold patches from training data.

reponse.texte: Le refactoring de code nécessite des modifications coordonnées préservant le comportement sur plusieurs fichiers, constituant un test plus difficile et réaliste des agents que ce que proposent les benchmarks actuels.
reponse.citation: Code refactoring, which requires coordinated, behavior-preserving changes across many files, offers a substantially harder and more realistic test of agent capability, yet remains underserved by current benchmarks.

reponse.texte: Les évaluations menées avec les modèles de pointe montrent que le meilleur agent n'atteint qu'un taux de résolution de 41,2 % sur les tâches de refactoring complexes de SWE-Bench ProMax.
